messages:
sophie: Follow-up to the ingress RFC  proposing a 'time-slice controller' for per-request budgets. idea: carry a small integer budget (ms) that drives admission, hedging, and graceful de-escalation for streaming. design goals: predictable SLO behavior, minimal header surface, survivable streaming checkpoints.
rahul: Nice. how does this interplay with tenant quotas and queuing? ie if a tenant is throttled can we still honor client deadlines?
sophie: We Compute slice = min(client_deadline_ms, tenant_allocated_window_ms). admission uses usual token-bucket; if tenant_allocated_window_ms is zero we backpressure/queue as today. key: slice is advisory for hedging/fallthrough only, not an auth token.
tom: Streaming concern: if upstream sends sporadic chunks over long time, we shouldn't kill the request as long as progress exists. how do you define progress?
sophie: Three-tier progress model: 1) framed progress events (preferred), 2) chunk bytes in last Ns, 3) explicit keepalive pings. If any of the above arrive we treat as forward progress and refresh a small amount on the slice (not exceed a cap). we avoid full resets to prevent gaming.
mei: Observability: add span tags `rw.slice_ms_at_ingress`, `rw.slice_remaining_ms`, and an event when hedges spawn. Also histograms: `rw.slice_remaining_ms{route,outcome}` and `rw.hedge_success_ratio{route}`. we'll want tenant-level percentiles and a per-route heatmap.
rahul: Billing/regression concern: hedges will double-run compute sometimes. we need traces to attribute cost to route+tenant so Optimize can suggest policy changes and we can alert on hedging-cost > X% of spend.
tom: gRPC bidi and midstream failover: if we spawn a hedge midstream we can be duplicating partial outputs. solution: require a lightweight idempotency/resume token header from clients when they want safe midstream hedging; otherwise hedges are disabled for bidi streams. KV-cache note: partial response keys need a finalized key only when stream finishes or explicit commit.
sophie: Implementation sketch: header `x-rw-time-slice-ms` numeric; for gRPC streaming add binary meta `rw-time-slice-ms`. header is immutable once ingress sets it; proxies must not increase it. on an upstream response progress boundary we emit a small trailer `x-rw-slice-left-ms` if TLS/http trailers supported, else an ingress event in trace. pseudocode: 
```
start = now()
slice = compute_slice_ms(req)
while not finished:
  if progress_event():
    slice = min(slice, slice + refresh_delta, slice_cap)
  if now() - start > slice:
    if allow_fallbacks:
      trigger_fallback()
    else:
      abort_request()
  record_metric("rw.slice_remaining_ms", slice - (now()-start))
```
mei: Rollout plan: feature flag `time_slice.controller` default OFF, enable for 5% canaries for 1 week, collect hedging rate, false-abort rate, and per-tenant cost impact. dashboard proto ready on my side.
rahul: Config knobs: per-tenant `time_slice_mode = {off, latency_sensitive, cost_sensitive}` where latency_sensitive biases hedging earlier, cost_sensitive raises hedge threshold and prefers fallbacks. also `progress_refresh_cap_ms` to limit client refresh abuse.
tom: Ops: ensure we don't leak the header back to clients in proxied responses, and that retries from clients don't get an inflated slice. instrument tests: one for slow-chunked stream that should survive, one for malicious keepalive flood that should not inflate slice beyond cap.
deploy-bot: rollout checklist added: feature flag `time_slice.controller` (OFF), telemetry opt-in, unit + integration tests, doc PR. tagging owners: @sophie @mei @rahul. :white_check_mark:
sophie: I'll update the RFC with these details and open the feature-flag PR + test harness. any objections to landing the draft and starting the canary?
mei: No objections. I'll wire mock metrics and the dashboard.
rahul: SGTM. keep an eye on hedging cost alerts.
